requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Backgrounds read as warm white, product image wells as white, headings as pine green #264C43, and information panels as cream #F5F0E6. Allow ordinary rendering and display differences, but fail a visibly different heading color, panel color or background system.

Each main image identifies its own kit by the correct name, code and USD 24 price. Each shopping card presents both complete records, with USD 24 visibly associated with each individual kit. Swapped names or codes, missing prices, or a price presented as buying both kits fail.

Where a full motif is visible, Fern Study has one upright curved stem and six opposite leaf pairs; Daisy Study has three eight-petal flowers, each with a stem and two leaves. Preprinted and partial views retain the same underlying design. Cropped material or stitch details need not expose the entire motif, but visible elements must agree with their SKU. Missing, extra or substituted motif elements fail.

Full motifs occupy a 100 × 100 mm design area relative to the supplied 150 mm inner hoop diameter and 250 × 250 mm fabric. Use visible component relationships or dimension annotations as evidence; permit perspective and close-up cropping. A full motif visibly enlarged or reduced to an incompatible physical scale fails. Printing a dimension on every image is not required.

The three specifications occupy the initial process stage and each records #264C43, the 150 mm inner hoop diameter and all three exact purchase labels. The one-page hierarchy table states selling points, priorities, placements and minimum text sizes. The shot list assigns all nineteen images and the video their roles, proportions and required content. The variant table accurately compares both names, codes, individual USD 24 prices, component and motif dimensions, motif differences and recorded thread assignments. Omitted entries or contradictions with the client records fail.

Each image fulfills its assigned role and content. Both mains and cards carry the exact brand and tagline with correct applicable SKU records; one card compares motifs and the other compares supplied materials and variant fabrics. Use square mains, 2:3 detail panels and 9:16 cards, with an upper 20% information band, lower 80% white product well, 5% outer margins and text height at least 3% of the shorter side. Typography stays in the band. Each main uses the specified heading color and a product group spanning 85–90% of the well's width. Each tabletop image prepares its corresponding kit for starting work. Missing role-specific content or incompatible relative geometry fails.

For each kit independently, the inventory accounts for one hoop, one matching preprinted cotton square, four skeins, two No. 7 needles, one guide and one box. Inventory and material records cover 150/166 mm hoop diameters, 250 × 250 mm fabric, 38 mm needles, a 100 × 140 mm guide and a 270 × 270 × 35 mm box; each inventory explicitly dimensions its hoop, fabric and guide and repeats the specified inner diameter. Each material panel shows cotton weave and the needle pair and lists T01 Pine #365744, T02 Sage #90A889, T03 Cream #F3E9D2 and T04 Ochre #C99236, each 8 m and six-strand. The hoop, fabric and guide share a physical scale in each inventory and retain their relative sizes on each tabletop. Perspective is allowed; missing records, cross-SKU fabric substitutions or incompatible sizes fail.

Both instructions order mounting, separating two strands and threading, stitching, and trimming/gathering the back, with a visible two-from-six strand separation. Close-ups name stem, satin and straight stitches and follow the records: Fern has an Ochre stem in stem stitch, Sage left and Pine right leaves in satin stitch, and Cream veins in straight stitch; Daisy has Pine stems in stem stitch, Sage leaves, Cream petals and Ochre centers in satin stitch, and Pine leaf veins in straight stitch. Working strands number two. Both state panels begin with complete gray unstitched outlines. Fern's partial state has its stem and bottom three leaf pairs completed, with the upper three pairs outlined; completion fills and veins all twelve leaves. Daisy's partial state completes only the left flower, its stem and two leaves; completion finishes all three flowers, stems and six leaves. Incorrect assignments, partial-state placement, counts or sequence fail.

Both finished panels, both cards and the purchase panel associate completed work with 'Finished example - stitch it yourself'; each card clearly labels each kit's completed example. Scissors in both instructions, both tabletops and the purchase panel carry 'You supply: scissors'. The purchase panel distinguishes supplied goods, buyer-owned scissors and completed outcomes in three labeled groups, repeating the specification wording exactly. Under 'In your kit', it accounts per kit for one hoop, one matching fabric square, four skeins, two needles, one guide and one box. A shared stock presentation is acceptable if per-kit quantities and variant fabrics remain unambiguous. Missing labels or stock, ambiguous label placement or a suggestion that finished embroidery is supplied fails.

Review the entire ten-second video. It covers both kits, their shared supplied contents, visible two-strand preparation and both completed outcomes. It identifies Fern Study / EK-01 / USD 24 and Daisy Study / EK-02 / USD 24 as individual sale records, and labels each completed outcome 'Finished example - stitch it yourself'. Product identities, motif structures and thread assignments remain compatible with the references and corresponding final images. Shot order and transitions may vary; missing kit coverage, incorrect facts, unlabeled outcomes or a different duration fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least ten pages and visibly reuses every specification document and all nineteen final images. It includes three stills identifiable as frames from the delivered video. Resizing and editorial cropping are acceptable when source identity remains clear. A fact-mapping page links brand colors, quantities, dimensions, exact wording and SKU differences to named visuals. Missing source coverage, substituted artwork, insufficient video stills or incomplete fact mapping fails.
